sources.title: CDC: Managing Insulin in an Emergency

base.text: Water: plan one gallon per person per day, for several days.
base.note: You cannot carry all of it. A filter or bleach covers the gap.

base.text: Non-perishable food, a several-day supply.
Manual can opener.
Battery-powered or hand-crank radio, or a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert.
Flashlight and extra batteries.
First aid kit.
Whistle, to signal for help.
Dust mask, to help filter contaminated air.
Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape, to shelter in place.
Moist towelettes, garbage bags and plastic ties for personal sanitation.
Wrench or pliers, to turn off utilities.
Local maps.
Cell phone with chargers and a backup battery.
Soap, hand sanitizer, disinfecting wipes and personal hygiene items.
Non-prescription medications, such as pain relievers, anti-diarrhea medication, antacids or laxatives.
Prescription eyeglasses and contact lens solution.
Cash.
Copies of insurance policies, ID and bank account records, in a waterproof container or saved electronically.
A written list of family and emergency contacts.
base.note: Your phone may be dead or lost.

base.text: Sleeping bag or warm blanket.
A complete change of clothing for your climate, and sturdy shoes.
Matches in a waterproof container.
Paper and pencil.

ifT1D.text: Aim for **at least a week** of diabetes supplies in this kit.
ifT1D.note: CDC says 1 to 2 weeks. ADA says at least a week. Use kit supplies day to day and replace them before they expire.

ifT1D.text: Keep the T1D kit in a waterproof bag or container that is easy to spot and easy to grab.
Insulin for every injection you might need (rapid-acting, and long-acting backup if your plan includes it).
Syringes or pen needles.
Pump users: spare infusion sets, cartridges, reservoirs or pods, and insertion devices.
A cooler bag or evaporative cooling pouch (keep insulin cool, never frozen).
An empty container for safely carrying used syringes, needles and lancets.
Blood glucose meter and extra batteries.
Test strips and lancets with a lancing device.
Ketone strips.
Spare CGM sensors, and a way to charge the receiver or phone.
Extra batteries for the pump.
Alcohol wipes.
Glucose tablets or 15 grams of fast carbs (juice, hard candy or honey), in several places.
Glucagon, in date, with the people around you knowing where it is.
Snacks with protein and carbohydrate.
Copies of all prescriptions, including eye prescriptions.
A list of current medicines, doses and the times you take them.
Pump settings: basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, glucose target and correction factors (print the saved plan from this app).
Names, addresses and phone numbers of the pharmacy and doctors.
Make, model and serial number of the pump and CGM.
Copies of photo ID and health insurance card.
A medical ID bracelet or necklace, worn.

ifMeds.text: Each of this person's medications (listed below).
ifMeds.note: Pack the medicines themselves, not only the list.

ifMeds.text: A written list of this person's medications, doses and the times they take them.
The pharmacy and doctor names and phone numbers, written down.

ifChild.text: If the child is an infant: formula, bottles, diapers, wipes and diaper rash cream.
Books, games, puzzles or other activities.

ifPet.text: Food: a several-day supply, in an airtight, waterproof container.
Water: a water bowl and several days' supply of water.
An extra supply of any regular medication, in a waterproof container.

ifPet.note: Ask your veterinarian what is best for your pet.

ifPet.text: Collar, ID tag and harness or leash, plus a backup leash, collar and ID tag.
Copies of the pet's registration and other records, in a waterproof container and also saved electronically.
A travel bag, crate or sturdy carrier, ideally one per pet.
Litter and litter box if needed, newspapers, paper towels, plastic trash bags and household chlorine bleach.
A picture of you with your pet, to help prove ownership if you are separated.
Favorite toys, treats or bedding to reduce stress.
Microchip the pet and keep the contact information current.
ifPet.note: Include an emergency contact outside your immediate area.
